I took a gig last month, it was a pretty long one this time. Two what I guess we could call long weeks things were kinda weird. The system was pretty small just a few planets around a white dwarf, pretty spectacular little system actually. There were some supernovae in the backdrop bright orange red and yellow clouds lit up the entire sky reflecting the brilliant white starlight. I gotta say, it was quite the sight.

Well, we landed all fine enough no big problems, one of the landing gears got bent and the techs got on it right after we set up base camp. Gotta pretty big crew this gig, 40 guys so I took it solo, we had a supply drop scheduled for a week in. I say scheduled because it never fuckin' happened. So we're on this goddamn rock with no food. I managed to stretch the rations out for a few days, but I didn't bring a whole lot so they went pretty quick.

Anyways long story short here I told the command what was up and they were in just the same jam, they were running low on some supplies, we took some hits on the first week from some stampedes. No deaths but some guys got pretty beat up, like coma beat up. They were fine once we got to the closest station and got patched up properly. But that's not really the story here this time, what is, is what we had to do those last few days. It was rough guys were grumpy everyone was pretty low.

So I got command to give me 5 guys and some ammo, I had my own gear and we set off for a little, hunt. I wasn't too sure what we should go after we had our choices. We wound up bagging a few bipedal what I'm gonna call “sheep”. Not big buggers but big enough, about 5 kg of meat from each one. Brown fleece on these guys is pretty too, its not curly but strait and doesn't knot. They seem to have a gland that greases them and lets the water bead off or something. I'm not a bio-tech guy, but hey I cut em open. We saw lots of the little suckers eatin; lichen and stuff around pools of water here. Wound up netting a bunch at once. Bitey guys I tell you. Got me pretty good, they got these plates and kinda duckbills too, but big wide ones almost like a cartoon. Kinda cute in a way.

So we bagged those guys put em down, and got to butchering, that brought the big guys out to play. So here I am elbow deep in the guts of these poor little guys that are gonna be steak dinner(pretty tender too) and out of some bush comes this behemoth. The damned thing was about 20 meters long and 10 tall, quadrupedal. Big ol sharp teeth on em, two rows kinda like a shark. Skins on em were kinda scraggly but shiny, hard as hell too. One of the crew opened up on em with a carbine and they turned tail, well we thought they did. Smart bastards flanked around and caught us again!

There were about 10 or so of em but once we dropped one, they took off for good. We got our shit together and met back up with the rest of the crew. The cook-off went well, steaks were good. The big guy we dropped was worth it. Fed us strait on through till we got to the lz and had to leave some of him behind. I kept some plates of his hide as a trophy. Really lightweight for the size, about half a meter tall and maybe three quarters wide. Only weighs about a kilo, kinda purple red, almost a brown on the outside, shiny as can be. Kinda fleshy white on the inside, they were kinda part of a 3 layered armor skin. With a second layer made of smaller plate, and a third of a white membrane that was real tough. Hardly cut it with our knives.

Funny thing is, none of em really stank on the inside. Sometimes you get a beast that just makes you wanna toss it in a fire and burn it to ash. These guys had no smell at all. The meat was better than I've had in years. Makes a guy wanna go back, stock up on some meat for later, wonder what that crew was lookin' for there. Wasn't much there really, just some flora and fauna. And lots of water.

They did find something, not that I know what. Got real excited too. Poor little planet is probably just a hollow husk now. Shame really. The meat was good.

Eat well kids.

No-one should be able to be a reddit mod and a voat mod.

You do realize that there are a lot of people on Reddit who have nothing to do with the stuff going on over there, and run their subreddits and pretty much mind their own business, yes?

Also, I don't think it would do a lot to convince people to come over at all. If anything it's deliberately making it an official rivalry, which I doubt would do anything to help Voat, and probably make the site administration look like a bunch of jerks.

Plus, some reddit mods who come over here and want to continue to moderate may not even want to moderate the same subject as their subreddit.

Moderating isnt a secret art, curated by a specialist elite. It's basic and simple and anyone can do it. As a result, why allow a small group of people to moderate two major 'front pages of the internet' and perpetuate a gatekeeper stranglehold? Why not allow choice and diversity in moderation?

The same could be said of surgery or just about anything else, if you don't particularly care about the results.

However, if you want to do it RIGHT, moderating can take a lot of discretion, restraint, observation, diplomacy, often domain expertise, attention, time, effort, and a lot of other things that it takes to be a leader, at least if the subverse is at all sizeable. This does not mean that it is secret art, no, but it isn't something a potted plant can do unless you want a crappy job made of it. Leadership in online communities is a stressful experience, usually comes with no pay, and can result in you being hated and harassed quite a bit, even if you try to do right.

But the question was not the skill of the moderator, but the person of the moderator, and it seems like this is people being singled out and jumped on, many of which did not necessarily do anything wrong or harmful or were even near the censorship clusterfucks. That is not a good way to start a site that is supposed to be the alternative to reddit - by immediately sticking a scarlet letter on some people for being associated with those who are deemed unfavorable by the elite. It's a great way to drag the dirty laundry from there to stink up the place here.

If there's someone over there pulling shit with their moderator status (and I am aware that there are many, hence why we're here), then by all means they should not have a chance to spread their attitude here. However, the simple attribute of being a subreddit moderator should not be a criteria to cut someone off from moderation on Voat, especially since that ALSO discourages transparency - the people you'd need to worry about likely have no qualms getting an account with a completely different username, wriggle back into position, and start subtly plying their opinion undetected for months or years, if they are indeed ever found out at all.

We fundamentally disagree. Choice and diversity is good for a society. Allowing the first movers and those with a vested interest to corner another burgeoning forum of free speech is missing a critical opportunity. There is not one right way to moderate. Passivity just paves the way for Voat to be another forum exploited and gamed by a small cluster of self-interested self-referential people.

I don't know what you're using, but I'm going to assume Android, so here are some Android apps:

  • Hanafuda KOI KOI -- A digital version of a Japanese card game where you match specific types of cards for points. You may have seen these cards on Club Nintendo, the anime Summer Wars, or the DS game Clubhouse Games.
  • KAMI -- A game where you are trying to make the entire screen all one color. Pretty chill, actually.
  • Android Troper -- A TV Tropes app. Probably the best one I've ever found.
  • Puzzle and Dragons -- A game where you match icons to make your little Pokemon-knockoffs of the same color attack. You've probably heard of this due to Puzzle and Dragons Z + Super Mario Bros. Edition.
  • Crystal Defenders -- A spinoff of the Final Fantasy Tactics series, except it's a tower defense now. The pointer in the game may be a little off, but you get used to it. Actually quite fun as far as tower defense games go.
  • Robot Unicorn Attack 2 -- A game where you run and jump as long as possible while being a badass unicorn. You've probably heard of this one, but don't skip it because it's free. You NEED those wishes!
  • Doodle God -- A game where you match elements to create a sinless world.
  • Doodle Devil -- A game where you match elements to create a sinful world.
  • Any of the official Doodle God/Devil spinoffs -- Basically the same as Doodle God/Devil.
  • Fantasy Defense -- A fun tower defense game that's really challenging right off the bat. The only catch is that all the females seem to have giant boobs. Don't worry, though, you can only tell during the full-art title screen sequence.
  • Shizuku Talk -- An app where you watch an anime girl animated beautifully with a semi-new animation technology (I think this app is a test for it). She talks about her life, what she's been doing, etc. If you don't understand Japanese, skip this game.
  • Tiny Tower -- A game where you build up a tower. You can actually share your tower with others, too.
  • Lyne -- A game where you have to connect two boxes of the same color with lines, and you can't overlap lines of a different color. Extremely difficult once you get out of the first set of puzzles. I'm still not to set three and I've been playing for a few months.
